headline: Audits show design-model confidence, benchmarks, and screen rankings fail to certify outcomes
label: Reliability Audits For Biological Design
summary: New audits quantify when conformal guarantees, predicted confidence, and screen-derived rankings break down in CRISPR, siRNA, and protein design pipelines.
synthesis: The dominant thread is stress-testing whether design-pipeline outputs license claims about candidate sequences. The conformal selection analysis finds public CRISPR off-target cohorts (10 guides) fall orders of magnitude short of the ~20,000 needed for finite-sample certification, and documents CIRCLE-seq grouping leakage plus free baselines that match learned selectors. A protein language model audit reports a steering cliff and shows ESMFold predicted confidence and activation-based gates cannot certify generate-and-screen outcomes. TRACE demonstrates that CRISPRi rejuvenation rankings shift with the aging cohort chosen and largely track proliferation programs, while Perturb-seq transfer work shows knockdown responses do not move cleanly across four cell lines without partial screening of each, motivating the set-based CASTER adaptation. Constructive counterparts, Silscore's positional nearest-neighbour siRNA potency model and DeepRNAi's on/off-target predictor with a released benchmark, pair modelling with explicit external-transfer evaluation rather than in-distribution scores.
